name: clickhouse-2a6274d2

policy.because: Single node with three platform updates already queued against deadlines, so a restart here competes with maintenance Aiven will run anyway.

freeze.reason: Data Innovation Summit. The project is on stage, so nothing changes unattended, however good the reason.

contacts.why: Last touched it: changed it 3 times in the event log
Last touched it: changed it 2 times in the event log

ownership: Observed, not declared: Marmot's asset_owners and teams tables are empty, so these are the people Aiven lists as contacts and the people the event log shows changing this service.

findings.title: Reachable from 0.0.0.0/0
findings.detail: The ip filter allows every address, so the only thing between this service and the internet is its password.

runbook.title: Close the service to the open internet
steps: List what actually connects: the integrations in this catalog plus any application using a service credential.
Collect the egress ranges those clients come from. A guess here locks out production.
Replace the ip_filter with that list using aiven_service_update, leaving 0.0.0.0/0 out.
Keep your own access in the list, or you lock yourself out along with everyone else.
runbook.whileItRuns: Established connections survive. New connections from anything outside the list are refused immediately, which is the whole point and also the risk.
runbook.rollback: Reversible: put the previous filter back with the same call.
runbook.verify: Connect from an allowed address, then from one that is not. The second attempt must fail, or the filter did not take.

findings.title: One node, so a restart is an outage
findings.detail: There is nothing to fail over to. Every restart, plan change and platform update is downtime that has to be timed rather than absorbed.

runbook.title: Restart a service that has no second node
steps: Treat this as planned downtime and announce it, because that is what it is.
Check no platform maintenance is already in flight for the same service.
Prefer the existing maintenance window over a restart of your own.
Restart, then watch the dependents rather than the service: it comes back before they do.
runbook.whileItRuns: A total outage for the length of the restart. Change data capture stops and resumes from its replication slot; consumers downstream fall behind rather than lose data.
runbook.takes: A few minutes, most of it the service coming back up.
runbook.rollback: None. A restart cannot be undone, only waited out.
runbook.verify: Service state RUNNING, the CDC connector back to RUNNING, and consumer lag falling across two readings rather than one.

findings.title: 3 platform updates queued, the first due 2026-09-22
findings.detail: After each deadline Aiven applies the update itself. On a single node that is downtime at a time nobody chose. Earliest: Tiered storage zero copy improvements. Fixes a metadata leak in tiered storage.

runbook.title: Apply platform maintenance before its deadline
steps: Read the deadlines from aiven_service_get: after them, Aiven applies the update whether or not it suits you.
Pick a window before the earliest deadline and inside the service maintenance window.
Apply the updates there, oldest deadline first.
runbook.whileItRuns: Rolling on a multi-node service, downtime on a single node. Either way it is the same interruption you would get by leaving it to the deadline, but at a time you chose.
runbook.takes: Minutes per update, longer for a version upgrade.
runbook.rollback: A version upgrade is one way. Plan for going forward, not back.
runbook.verify: The pending update list is empty and the service reports the new version.

findings.title: CPU spikes on an otherwise idle service
findings.detail: 55% peak against a 8% average. That is work arriving in bursts, not a service running out of headroom, and it is not a reason to change the plan.

findings.title: Termination protection is off
findings.detail: Nothing stands between a deletion call and this service, which is a cheap gap to close.

runbook.title: Turn on termination protection
runbook.whileItRuns: Nothing. It is a configuration flag, with no restart.
runbook.rollback: Reversible with the same call, which is exactly why it is worth having on.
runbook.verify: Read the service back and confirm the flag is set.

plan.note: No plan prices were captured for clickhouse, so a fix here cannot state its cost yet.
